note: Both sets capture the dishwasher temperature thresholds, capacity, sensor redundancy, and the clothes-drying weight-based scoring bands, and both repeat several facts under two names (heated drying, cycle completion, wash/rinse cycles, and the drying thresholds stated twice). Set A additionally captures the important laundry eligibility condition (complete, uninterrupted washer cycle) that Set B omits entirely. However, A also adds a claim reading the Figure 8 axis ticks 90/100/110/120 as 'points', when the figure shows those numbers on the % of original weight (x) axis and the y axis (points per clothes drying task) is unlabeled. On balance A recovers a substantive rule B misses at the cost of one misbound figure claim.
remarks: Both sets duplicate the same facts under alternate attribute names (e.g., 'required temperature sensor peak' vs 'temperature sensor minimum value', 'heated drying option | status' vs 'dishwasher | heated drying option', 'cycle completion signal' vs 'cycle completion confirmation', 'clothes-drying points | scoring value' vs 'clothes-drying task | scoring criteria'), inflating both claim counts. The Figure 8 y-axis (points per clothes drying task) has no numeric tick labels in the image, so any claim assigning point values to 90-120 is unsupported; the text layer also scrambles the figure's axis labels. Neither set extracts the temperature-of-record rule (higher of two sensor readings, or lower if the higher sensor is defective) or the definition of cycle interruption.
